date: 2026-09-03
notes: v54 = inferred types for inline vars (God directive mtkt2shb). An untyped INTEGER initialiser now infers NativeInt instead of LongInt -- `var i := -1` is 8 bytes on a 64-bit app, 4 on a 32-bit one -- and the same rule now drives an inferred `for var i := ...` counter. Only types narrower than NativeInt are widened, so Int64/QWord keep their width; explicit casts like byte(10) are still never promoted. A string/char literal initialiser now infers exactly what a bare `string` means at that point: wide under -Mdelphiunicode/-Munleashed (unchanged from v53, which already did this) and ShortString under $H- (which v53 got wrong). Compiler-binary-only refresh on top of v53; only compiler/defutil.pas and compiler/pstatmnt.pas changed. No PPU format, RTL or package change -- UNITS ARE STILL THE v52 SET, so an existing v52/v53 units install stays valid and auto-update.bat can take the ~3.4 MB bin alone. Verified on Linux: 45-assertion NativeInt matrix over 13 structural contexts and a 20-assertion string matrix over $H+/$H- both go from baseline failures to 0 under BOTH -Munleashed and -Mdelphiunicode; full 2098-test corpus with a nondeterminism control shows ZERO unintended regression; self-host fixpoint byte-identical. NOT verified: Win64 runtime (no wine on the build host). BREAKING-ish: code that relied on an inferred integer being exactly 4 bytes (a `var LongInt` argument, or LongInt-vs-Int64 overload choice) must now name the type explicitly.
